During last night's large-scale Russian missile attack on Ukraine, the interception rate of Kh-101 cruise missiles was unusually low - one of the lowest so far this year. 
Out of roughly 48 Kh-101 cruise missiles launched, I could only confirm around 10 interceptions, mainly by fighter jets. 
In my opinion, this was caused by Ukraine's ongoing F-16 maintenance crisis, and due to the fact that Russia is striking areas of Ukraine closer to the border, providing Ukrainian air defences with much less time to shoot down the missiles. The missiles also flew in very large groups immediately towards their targets, without changing course much, completely overwhelming Ukrainian air defences. 
The Kh-101s impacted three cities - Kremenchuk (Poltava Oblast), Pryluky (Chernihiv Oblast), and Oleksandriya (Kirovohrad Oblast).
Most of the impacts occurred in Kremenchuk, while around a dozen occurred in Oleksandriya, along with another dozen or so in Pryluky. Multiple different locations in Kremenchuk, including the hydroelectric power plant, were hit. 
The interception rate on Kalibrs was much higher (roughly 9 out of 12 missiles were shot down), with the remaining 3 striking two different targets in Kremenchuk.
As for ballistics, patriot systems in Kyiv shot down ~4 out of 10 Iskander-M/RM-48U S-400 missiles, and air defences near the city of Ukrainka in Kyiv Oblast shot down both Oniks-M supersonic cruise missiles targeting the Trypillya Thermal Power Plant. The 2 Zircons both impacted Trypillya TPP.

events.text:
📊 Syria to serve as Iraq’s oil route to bypass Hormuz – but volumes remain a drop in the bucket
The Iraqi government has asked Syria to help with crude oil exports, Yousef Qiblawy, chief executive officer of the state-owned Syrian Petroleum Co., told Bloomberg.
Iraq already sends some of its fuel oil to Syria’s Mediterranean port of Baniyas by truck, with around 1,000 vehicles making the journey each day, each carrying roughly 220 barrels, Qiblawy said.
He noted that the same or even a larger number of trucks loaded with crude could pass through Syria.
The export of Iraqi crude to Syria by truck could begin as early as mid-October, according to Qiblawy.
Iraq also transits some crude and fuel oil through Jordan to avoid the dangerous Strait of Hormuz. Reuters reported last week that Iraq’s state-owned Oil Tanker Company had also managed to transport 2 million barrels of Iraqi crude aboard a very large crude carrier (VLCC) through the strait.
Based on the figures cited by Qiblawy, trucks passing through Syria would carry 220,000 barrels of oil per day, or between 6.6 million and 6.82 million barrels per month. That's a far cry from the 93 million barrels per month that Iraq routinely exported through the Strait of Hormuz before the Iran war, according to numbers cited by Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Mohammed in May.

✡️🔯 Mossad’s Flydubai security lapse puts Israelis’ US visa waiver at risk
Israelis could reportedly lose their visa-free entry to the US over safety failures involving Flydubai, the Times of Israel reports.
A US delegation is due to visit Israel to review its compliance with the security requirements of the US Visa Waiver Program, which Israel joined in 2023. Under the program, Israel is required to review information on all passengers and aircrew arriving in the country.
Israeli government officials had received the passenger and crew list for the notorious Flydubai Flight 1073 in advance, Haaretz reported earlier. The list included the Omani co-pilot accused of carrying out the attack.
The suspect, identified as 29-year-old Hamam Al Hammami, had been flagged as a security risk as early as 2024 when he was working as a co-pilot trainee for Oman Air. Despite being found in possession of extremist material, he was allowed to continue working for the airline in an administrative role, according to ABC News.
Israel’s Transportation Ministry and Mossad were responsible for vetting the crew list, Haaretz points out. This raises questions about how the Israeli intelligence agency failed to flag Al Hammami before the flight and allowed him to board the aircraft.
👉The controversy adds to mounting reports that the Israeli government, led by Benjamin Netanyahu, was warned of an impending Hamas attack but that the prime minister failed to pass the warning on to Israeli security officials.
